'Left rail' means the portal icon rail in the gas and umbrella videos and the micro-app's own menu in weather and lightning. The captures show weather and gas items inside the Connected Environment menu.

Umbrella chapter bars 'Connected Environment > Weather Station, Lightning, Gas' (chapters 2 and 3) read as one menu holding all three. No frame has all three. Projects A, B and C each hold different products, and the umbrella itself says 'Switched on per project'.

Every spec has the same title 'Connected Environment'. The eyebrows differ: Weather 'WEATHER STATION', Lightning 'LIGHTNING . CONNECTED ENVIRONMENT', Gas 'GAS . CONNECTED ENVIRONMENT'. Weather alone drops the umbrella tag.

Weather lane is labelled three ways. Umbrella: 'WIRELESS MESH . MODBUS STYLE FRAMES', steps 'on-site radio network / decoded and stored / Weather Station readings and status'. Weather video: 'ON-SITE MESH', steps 'on the site / decode and store / WakeCap reads and serves'. Lightning video: 'WIRELESS MESH' with no Modbus. The weather and lightning videos never mention it, and the lightning video's diagram says 'WIRELESS MESH' only. The Modbus explanation is on first use in the umbrella as required and word for word as the guardrail has it. Gas cadence is hedged differently. Umbrella states it plainly in narration and the diagram: 'detectors report ... about every half hour', 'WakeCap checks it about every minute'. Gas video softens it: 'every minute or so', 'often half an hour apart'. The gas diagram omits the half hour figure that the umbrella diagram has. G03 is live_today unknown. Pick one hedge.

'Blackline' is first named in the umbrella k04 as page text with no gloss, before the paths section introduces 'vendor'. The gas video glosses it once ('the gas vendor', g11) before the paths diagram. Umbrella viewers meet the name unexplained.

The acknowledge and close statement is hedged differently. Umbrella k04: 'the page says acknowledging or closing is recorded here, with who and when'. Gas g11 states it plainly. 'You and your team stay in control' (umbrella z01) repeats a04 'People stay in control'.

Opening hooks all use the same template: a scene, then a question ('Is it safe ...? Where do you look first?', 'The supervisor asks, so what now?', 'What warns the crew first?', 'How would you know?'). Closings all use 'Your next step' (lightning, gas) or 'Next time ... open' (weather) and a 'What is new' list card in three of four. Four videos in a row sound alike.

The captions of a02 and a04 are in present tense ('An assistant proposes. coverage_of_user_brief.note: Story is clearly stronger. Each has a concrete hook and one thesis ('A heat number is not an answer', 'what warns the crew first', 'silence is not calm', 'where do you look first'). Spec check passes and lengths are 2:22 to 3:21 at the tool's pace, with the umbrella and weather at the upper limit. Visuals are improved with zooms, spotlight callouts and diagrams, but still weak in places. Tri scenes (umbrella o03, s01, c02; lightning l11) leave the lower half black. Path diagrams (weather w16 to w17, lightning l12 to l13, gas g14 to g15) are a thin strip in a large empty frame. Weather has four consecutive dense Settings pages (about 40 s), gas has six table-heavy beats, the lightning map beats show a blur. The four openings and closings share one template, so the set sounds samey. Voice cannot be judged without the real run, and word counts are at the 2.5 minute ceiling so real pace may overrun.
